summary: Speed one signed retry within the recent authenticated peer’s 30-second recovery window

replay.detail: No graph replay or admission-format change. A request whose response headers were lost can be retried through the existing idempotent replication receive path; an isolated accepted-but-lost-response control verifies one stored claim after the retry.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, migrations or persisted recovery credit. Credit is local per-peer process memory and starts absent after restart.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules/digests or coordinated member upgrade. Existing overload, membership removal and Fabric refusal cooldown policy remains in force.

compatibility.detail: Within five minutes of a successful authenticated outbound HTTP exchange, a route with genuinely newer local authority can use one jittered early signed attempt after a typed pre-headers transport failure and bounded HEAD probe. This speeds a recent peer's existing 30-second retry cap toward a probe interval of roughly 3–4 seconds. The five-minute epoch/probe eligibility is unchanged, and rate-limited probes continue throughout eligible retry waits without a ten-probe cutoff; hour-scale absence retries are unchanged. Older-peer HEAD 405 is transport-only. Mixed versions retain wire/client/harness contracts and differ in recent recovery speed. Retained watch failures remain historically unattributed; no native field or deployed performance acceptance is claimed.

downtime.detail: For peers inside the five-minute authenticated epoch, recovery can resume from the existing 30-second cap after roughly 3–4 seconds of bounded probe plus jitter. Absences outside the five-minute eligibility window keep prior quiet backoff and do not obtain renewed credit. Existing successful-HEAD deadline caps remain active during eligible longer waits. Early failure retains the original retry deadline and accumulated counter. Original 10000 ms native read oracle unchanged; live restart-to-API/health and field recovery have not been measured.

manual.detail: No additional manual step, fleet coordination, configuration or store change for installations using the existing replication worker. Normal binary upgrade applies.

recovery.detail: A successful authenticated outbound exchange arms one in-memory allowance for that route/auth epoch. Route/auth changes invalidate it; cancellation or timeout after spending cannot refund it. Swapping back restores the prior retry timing without reversing a migration; no replay or native acceptance follows from a swap. Operator-visible local worker phases include recovery-granted, recovery-consumed and recovery-refused-cause/no-pending/route/spent; these are bounded progress observations, not delivery or live stack proof.
